products.name: Aisera
products.note: AI service management platform; autonomous service desk; enterprise governance features

reading.body:
Aisera builds an AI agent platform for automating routine business operations tasks like IT support, HR requests, and facilities scheduling, with named deployments showing up to 65 percent automation of incoming support requests.

The company positions itself as generative AI native and sells primarily on the ability to deploy agents without writing code, using natural language to configure task automation across enterprise channels. This is a narrow but mature use case: service desks and support functions are high-volume, repeatable work where each solved ticket has measurable business value, and where AI agents can be constrained to bounded domains. The deployments cited span transit agencies, professional services, logistics, and retail, suggesting the pattern generalizes.

For the grid constraint thesis, Aisera's relevance is indirect. These agents automate labor rather than requiring new compute infrastructure at deployment scale. The company appears to be a consumer of third-party models and compute rather than a builder of either, relying on proprietary and integrated large language models but not claiming novel training or infrastructure. This matters because it means Aisera's growth is downstream of the availability and cost of compute capacity, not a driver of new power or building demand.

The data does not cover Aisera's funding, valuation, customer count, revenue, or staffing, nor does it include independent verification of the automation rates cited or details on the proprietary model's training footprint.

profile_text.body:
Aisera is an enterprise software company that describes itself as focused on agentic AI for business operations. Its platform is positioned around deploying AI agents to automate service and support tasks across functions including IT, HR, facilities, and customer service. The company describes itself as a generative AI native company, and its site emphasizes use cases such as password resets, software provisioning, appointment scheduling, and field technician support across channels including Microsoft Teams, email, web portals, and mobile apps.

The core product is the Aisera AI agent platform, which the site describes as including an Agent Composer tool for building custom agents using natural language, an Aisera Assistant, and an Agent Assist capability for cross-domain workflow execution. The platform supports a proprietary large language model as well as integration of third-party models, with an LLM Studio component for tuning using organizational data. The site cites several named deployments: NJ Transit's internal agent named Travis for IT support, BDO Canada's self-service agent named EVA for IT task automation, OmniTRAX for unified employee support, Big 5 Sporting Goods for IT productivity, and Lifescan, where the company states that 65 percent of incoming support requests are now automatically resolved.

The held facts record Aisera as maintaining an AI service management platform with autonomous service desk and enterprise governance features, categorized under enterprise AI platforms and agent orchestration. No litigation, SEC filings, patents, or MCP server registrations are currently recorded for the company.
